source_text: However, the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child has clarified in communications, such as CRC/C/83/D/23/2017 (adopted March 2020), that while circumcision constitutes an interference with physical integrity, it does not per se violate the CRC if demonstrably in the child's best interests, assessed case-by-case; the committee rejected a blanket prohibition in that instance, weighing factors like cultural context and low complication rates (under 1% in controlled settings).
